testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which type of vehicle is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to roll over from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.

questions.explanation: Air brakes are effective and safe for stopping large, heavy vehicles when they are maintained and used correctly.

questions.question: When driving while pulling trailers, you should:

options.text: Make sudden turns with the steering wheel.
Push the accelerator to the floor when starting from a stop.

questions.explanation: Steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering moves can cause the trailer to tip over.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed near the front of a trailer.
Placed near the rear of a trailer.
Loaded with most weight on the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.explanation: To reduce rollover risk, spread cargo evenly across the trailer and keep the weight as low and centered as possible.

questions.question: Do not use the parking brake when parking if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.
There is water on the ground.

questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if the brakes are very hot from driving downhill or if they are wet in freezing weather. Hot brakes can be damaged by the parking brake. Wet brakes in freezing weather can ice over and lock the vehicle.

questions.question: Rollovers are most likely to happen when:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. Slow down before entering turns and curves, especially when the vehicle is fully loaded.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle goes around a corner:

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes.
The front and rear wheels will move in different paths.
It is best to allow the rear wheels to drive over the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels will move in different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. Trailers make this effect more noticeable.

questions.question: All tractors and trailers must be equipped with ABS.
questions.explanation: ABS is required on vehicles, trailers, and dollies made between 1997 and 1999, depending on the type of equipment.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle with dual air brakes, the air pressure must reach ____ before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up pressure to at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: Trailers built before 1975 are:

options.text: Not required to have spring brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not required to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are:

options.text: Only required when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, once air pressure is lost and spring brakes come on:

options.text: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use the spring brakes to drive normally.
The air tanks will refill automatically to a safe pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Pushing the correct control releases the spring brakes for a short time. This lets the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: When glad hands are coupled, the seals should be pressed together at a ____ angle.
questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, the seals should be pressed together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: A shut-off valve:

options.text: Is located on the front of a trailer.
Is located on the instrument panel.
Stops air from escaping the air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to prevent air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: When driving a combination rig, following distance should be:

options.text: Shorter than when driving a single vehicle.
About the same as when driving a single vehicle.
Longer than when driving a single vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Longer than when driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination rigs need longer following distances than single vehicles. They require more distance to stop.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, pressure of at least ____ should be built up in both brake systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build pressure of at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: The most common type of foundation brake used is the:
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: Brakes out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes out of adjustment will fail before properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment frequently to prevent problems.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used:

options.text: To make the air brakes work more effectively.
To temporarily release the spring brakes.
To charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To temporarily release the spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Pushing the correct control releases the spring brakes for a short time. This lets the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be:

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: Air tanks usually hold enough compressed air:

options.text: For one stop before needing to be refilled.
For several stops before needing to be refilled.
For a day's worth of braking.
For an unlimited number of stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: For several stops before needing to be refilled.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough compressed air for the brakes to work several times before they need to be refilled.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should not lose more than 4 psi of air pressure in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: The air entering air storage tanks may contain:
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the braking system, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. It is controlled by the air compressor governor.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Engage and disable the parking brake.
Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
Uncouple and recouple all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: After the system is charged, test the warning signal by rapidly pressing and releasing the brake pedal. This releases air from the system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.
